payload.name: EnumerateAllItemsForListQuestions
payload.description: When a user asks for a list of items (e.g., classes, courses, activities, hobbies) that a person took, attended, or is involved in, do not answer after finding one relevant memory; search multiple phrasings and memory kinds and aggregate all distinct items.
content: When a question asks for a list of items (e.g., 'what are the classes/courses/activities/hobbies'), treat it as an enumeration request: do not stop after the first supporting memory or after a single search.

Run multiple searches with varied phrasings and synonyms (e.g., class, course, workshop, training, seminar, activity) and include relevant memory kinds such as 'event', 'profile', and 'state'; for enrollments or sign-ups, include 'event' memories with future world_start if the query also covers planned or registered items.

Before answering, gather all distinct items from the combined retrieved set; if the retrieved set lacks enough distinct items or the question implies multiple, issue additional searches before finalizing.

solves: When a question asks to enumerate a person's items (e.g., classes taken, courses attended, activities, hobbies), the diagnosed failure was answering from the first retrieved memory only, missing other supported items. The reusable mechanism is that plural-list questions require multiple synonym searches and cross-kind evidence aggregation before answering. This applies to any future list-eliciting query about a person's activities, courses, or possessions, but not to questions seeking a single fact or a yes/no confirmation.
